function: Learned linear precoding and power allocation of RSMA common and private streams for LEO satellite downlink sum-rate maximization, using a parameterized quantum circuit (p. 1, 3-4).
system: LEO satellite BS, Nt = 12 antennas, N = 8 single-antenna ground stations (MISO, 1-layer RSMA), 28 GHz, Rician fading; no RIS (p. 2, 4-5).
method: Unsupervised quantum machine learning: parameterized quantum circuit, data re-uploading, L = 2, 512 shots, loss = negative sum rate, parameter-shift gradients, outputs mapped to WMMSE-style precoders (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Own LEO simulator: path loss, Rician fading, synthetic per-GS Doppler 100-1000 Hz; training and testing CSI generated independently, disjoint; no 3GPP model or measured data (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Disjoint training and testing CSI generated from the Doppler-variant LEO model; sum rate over 50 CSI realizations, SNR 0-20 dB, Nt = 12, N = 8 (p. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE, FP. Learned: UCML, a PyTorch CNN adopted from DCLPNN [6], trained with 200 and 10^4 samples (p. 1-2, 4).
metrics: Average sum rate (bps/Hz) versus SNR (Fig. 4), mean loss versus training epochs (Fig. 3), complexity orders (Table I), training-data size (p. 4-5).
complexity: Table I: UQML O(L Nqubit + N Nt^3); UCML, WMMSE and FP orders also listed; no runtime or parameter count (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "models small-scale Rician fading with a dominant line-of-sight (LoS) component"; the link is a custom model (Eq. 4 path loss, Eq. 5 synthetic Doppler), and no 3GPP TR 38.811 model or measured data is cited.
q2_support: p. 4: "All training and testing CSI samples Ndata are independently generated and disjoint."; this is a held-out split of the same model, Fig. 4 uses only Nt = 12 and N = 8, and no other scenario, antenna count, user count or Doppler range is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "Comparisons include: UQML, UCML, WMMSE, and FP"; p. 2: "unsupervised classical machine learning (UCML) adopted from [6]"; UCML is a CNN, and all are compared on sum rate in Fig. 4 (p. 4-5).
q4_support: p. 4: "Table I compares the algorithmic complexity of all four methods"; Table I gives O(L Nqubit + N Nt^3) for UQML.
q5_support: p. 4: "All training and testing CSI samples Ndata are independently generated and disjoint."; the CSI comes from the authors own simulator, and no code or data link, DOI or public dataset appears in the paper.
notes: Area 6, which wins over area 3: learned precoding and power control on a satellite downlink. The quantum circuit runs in IBM Qiskit, and p. 3: "with optimization currently performed on ground-based quantum processors". UCML counts as the learned baseline because it is a CNN adopted from DCLPNN [6]. The claim of generalization on p. 5: "strong generalization capabilities across diverse CSI realizations" refers to new realizations of the same model, so q2 is 0. Fig. 3 compares only convergence, and the sum-rate comparison is Fig. 4.
